propositions: The `transition` library function uses a fragmented force-bypass surface (force: bool, force_close: str, reason: str) that diverges from `claim` (force: str | None); both must converge on the universal canonical shape force: str | None where the string value carries the audit reason.

The transition CLI allows `--reason` to serve as the force-bypass audit note, but claim does not; this coupling must be removed so `--force[=<reason>]` is the sole force-note entry point across both verbs.

The concept of a force-bypass audit reason is spelled four different ways in-memory (force_reason, force_close, force_close_reason, force_plan_review); internal naming must unify to force_reason while retaining the persisted status_data key force_close_reason unchanged.
Legacy code calling transition(force_close='x') or transition(force=True) must map to the new force='x' / force='(no reason given)' signature with deprecation warnings via _deprecations.py.
Bare `--force` must normalize to '(no reason given)' identically on both claim and transition; empty-string force must be treated as present (not None) and normalized to the same placeholder.

Every guidance string (gates.py override hints, txn.py hints, transition.py help) currently shows either the decoupled `--reason`-as-force-note pattern or inconsistent spellings; all must show only `--force[=<reason>]` without any `--reason`-for-force wording.
